1-1.kid: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened at Kurukshetra, the holy field. His own people and the other side had gathered there, eager for battle. What did they do?

1-2.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Prince Duryodhana saw the other army lined up for battle. He went to his teacher and spoke to him.

1-3.kid: The prince tells his teacher to look at the mighty army on the other side. It was set in order by the son of Drupada, the teacher's own wise student.

1-4.kid: The prince goes on. On that side are heroes and mighty archers, as good in battle as Bhima and Arjuna. Drupada is there too, with his great chariot.

1-5.kid: The prince names more brave warriors on that side, among them Drishtaketu, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaivya, the best of men.

1-6.kid: He names still more: a strong warrior, Uttamaujas the brave, Saubhadra, and the sons of Draupadi. All of them fight from great chariots.

1-7.kid: Then the prince tells his teacher to hear the names of the chiefs and leaders of their own army, so that he will know them.

1-8.kid: The prince names them: his teacher himself, then Bhishma, Karna and Kripa, who win their battles, and Vikarna and others.

1-9.kid: He adds that many other heroes are there, well trained in war and armed with many kinds of weapons, ready to give their lives for his sake.

1-10.kid: The prince compares the two armies. His own army is led by Bhishma, and the army on the other side is led by Bhima.

1-11.kid: So he tells all his generals to stand firm in their places, each in their own part of the army, and to guard Bhishma.

1-12.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Bhishma, the grandfather and the oldest of the Kurus, blew his conch shell loudly, like a lion's roar, to cheer the prince.

1-13.kid: Sanjaya says that then conch shells, drums and horns all blared out at once, and the noise was huge.

1-14.kid: Then Krishna and Arjuna, standing in their great chariot pulled by white horses, blew their divine conch shells.

1-15.kid: Krishna blew his conch, and Arjuna blew his conch Devadatta. Vrikodara, who did terrible deeds, blew his mighty conch called Paundra.

1-16.kid: King Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew his conch Anantavijaya. Nakula and Sahadeva blew theirs, called Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

1-17.kid: Sanjaya names more great warriors there: a king with a great bow, the mighty Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, and an unbeaten warrior, among others.

1-18.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Drupada, the sons of Draupadi and the strong-armed Saubhadra all blew their own conch shells, on every side.

1-19.kid: That huge roar filled the earth and the sky, and it tore at the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra.

1-20.kid: Then Arjuna, whose sign was a monkey, saw the sons of Dhritarashtra lined up, with the shooting about to begin. He lifted his bow.

1-21.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Arjuna spoke to Krishna. Arjuna asks Krishna to stop his chariot in the middle, between the two armies.

1-22.kid: Arjuna wants to see the warriors standing there, eager for battle, and to know whom he must fight in this war.

1-23.kid: Arjuna wants to look at everyone gathered here to fight, who have come to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra in battle.

1-24.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Krishna did as Arjuna asked. He drove that finest of chariots into the middle, between the two armies.

1-25.kid: There, facing Bhishma, Drona and all the kings of the world, Krishna told Arjuna to look at all the Kurus gathered together.

1-26.kid: Then Arjuna saw who stood there: uncles and grandfathers, teachers, cousins, sons and grandsons, and friends.

1-27.kid: In both armies he saw his own family and friends, standing in their ranks. Seeing them all, Arjuna was filled with deep pity and spoke sadly.

1-28.kid: Arjuna, full of pity, spoke sadly. He tells Krishna that he sees his own family standing in their ranks, eager to fight.

1-29.kid: Arjuna says his arms and legs are giving way and his mouth is dry. His body is shaking, and his hair stands on end.

1-30.kid: Arjuna says his bow is slipping from his hand and his skin is burning. He cannot stand up straight, and his mind is spinning.

1-31.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that he sees bad signs. He cannot see any good coming from killing his own people in battle.

1-32.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna he does not want victory, or a kingdom, or pleasures. What good is a kingdom, or joy, or even life to them?

1-33.kid: Arjuna says the very people for whose sake they want a kingdom, joys and pleasures are standing here in battle, ready to give up their lives and riches.

1-34.kid: Arjuna says who they are: teachers, fathers, sons and grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives.

1-35.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that he does not want to kill them, even if they kill him. He would not do it to rule the three worlds, so how could he do it just for the earth?

1-36.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna what joy could come from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra. They have done wrong, he says, but killing them would only bring sin on his own side.

1-37.kid: So, Arjuna says, they should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, who are their own relatives. How could they be happy after killing their own family?

1-38.kid: Arjuna says that greed has clouded the minds of the people on the other side. They see nothing wrong in destroying a family, or in turning against friends.

1-39.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna why they should not turn away from such a sin, since they can clearly see the harm in destroying a family.

1-40.kid: Arjuna says that when a family is destroyed, its very old traditions die out. When the traditions are lost, wrongdoing takes over the whole family.

1-41.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that when wrongdoing takes over, the women of the family go wrong, and then the castes become mixed up.

1-42.kid: Arjuna says this mixing drags both the family and those who destroyed it to hell. Their ancestors fall too, because they no longer receive offerings of rice and water.

1-43.kid: Arjuna says that the wrong deeds of those who destroy families mix up the castes, and the old customs of caste and family are wiped out.

1-44.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna they have heard that people whose family customs have been destroyed must live in hell.

1-45.kid: Arjuna cries out that they are about to commit a great sin. They are ready to kill their own family, out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.

1-46.kid: Arjuna says it would be better for him if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, killed him in battle while he was unarmed and did not fight back.

1-47.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that after saying this on the battlefield, Arjuna threw aside his bow and arrows. He sank onto the seat of his chariot, his mind full of sorrow.

2-1.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Arjuna was overcome with pity and sorrow, his eyes full of tears. Then Krishna spoke these words to him.

2-2.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna where this sadness has come from at such a hard moment. He says it is not noble, it brings shame, and it closes the way to heaven.

2-3.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna not to give in to this weakness, because it does not suit him. He should throw off this mean loss of courage and stand up.

2-4.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna how he can shoot arrows in battle at Bhishma and Drona. They are people who deserve his deepest respect.

2-5.kid: Arjuna says it would be better to live as a beggar than to kill his great teachers. If he killed them, every pleasure he had would be stained with blood.

2-6.kid: Arjuna says he does not know which is better, that they win or that the other side wins. After killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, who face them now, he would not even want to live.

2-7.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that his heart is weak and his mind is confused about his duty. He asks Krishna to tell him clearly what is best. He offers himself as a student and asks to be taught.

2-8.kid: Arjuna says nothing can take away the sorrow that is drying up his senses. Not even ruling the whole earth without a rival, or ruling over the gods.

2-9.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Arjuna, the conqueror of his enemies, said to Krishna, 'I will not fight!' and then fell silent.

2-10.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that Krishna, as if smiling, spoke to the sorrowing Arjuna there, in the middle of the two armies.

2-11.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is sad for those who need no sadness, even while he speaks wise words. The truly wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

2-12.kid: Krishna says there was never a time when he did not exist, nor Arjuna, nor these kings. And none of them will ever stop existing in the future.

2-13.kid: Krishna says the one who lives in the body passes through childhood, youth and old age. In the same way, it passes on to another body. Calm, steady people are not troubled by this.

2-14.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that cold and heat, pleasure and pain, come when the senses touch things. They come and go and do not last. He should bear them bravely.

2-15.kid: Krishna says a calm person who stays the same in pain and pleasure, and is not troubled by them, is able to reach immortality.

2-16.kid: Krishna says what is unreal never exists, and what is real never stops existing. Those who know the truth have seen this about both.

2-17.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to know that the One that fills all this can never be destroyed. No one has the power to destroy it.

2-18.kid: Krishna says the bodies come to an end, but the Self who lives in them is eternal, cannot be destroyed and cannot be measured. So he tells Arjuna to fight.

2-19.kid: Krishna says that anyone who thinks the Self kills, or thinks it is killed, does not understand. The Self does not kill, and it is not killed.

2-20.kid: Krishna says the Self is never born and never dies, and it does not stop being. It is unborn and eternal. It is not killed when the body is killed.

2-21.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna this: if someone knows that the one who lives in the body can never be destroyed, is never born and never changes, how can that person kill, or make another kill?

2-22.kid: Krishna says that as a person throws away worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the one who lives in the body leaves worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

2-23.kid: Krishna says weapons cannot cut the Self. Fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.

2-24.kid: Krishna says the Self cannot be cut, burnt, wetted or dried. It lasts for ever, it is everywhere, it never changes and it does not move.

2-25.kid: Krishna says the Self is unseen, beyond thinking, and never changes. Knowing this, Arjuna should not grieve.

2-26.kid: Krishna says that even if Arjuna thinks of the one who lives in the body as always being born and always dying, he still should not grieve.

2-27.kid: Krishna says death is certain for whatever is born, and birth is certain for whatever dies. So Arjuna should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.

2-28.kid: Krishna says all beings are unseen at their beginning, seen in their middle, and unseen again at their end. So what is there to grieve about?

2-29.kid: Krishna says some people see the Self as a wonder. Others speak of it as a wonder, and others hear of it as a wonder. Yet even after hearing of it, people do not understand it.

2-30.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the one who lives in every body can never be harmed. So he should not grieve for any living being.

2-31.kid: Krishna says Arjuna should look at his own duty and not waver. For a warrior, nothing is better than a fight for what is right.

2-32.kid: Krishna says warriors are lucky when a fair battle like this comes to them without their asking. It is like an open door to heaven.

2-33.kid: Krishna says that if Arjuna refuses to fight in this fair war, he will throw away his duty and his honour, and he will bring sin on himself.

2-34.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that people will speak of his dishonour for ever. For someone who has been honoured, dishonour is worse than death.

2-35.kid: Krishna says the great chariot warriors will think Arjuna ran from the battle out of fear. Those who once thought highly of him will think little of him.

2-36.kid: Krishna says his enemies will say many unkind things and mock his strength. What could hurt more than that?

2-37.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that if he is killed, he will reach heaven. If he wins, he will enjoy the earth. So he should stand up, ready to fight.

2-38.kid: Krishna says to treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, winning and losing as the same, and then go into battle. That way Arjuna will not bring sin on himself.

2-39.kid: Krishna says he has explained one kind of wisdom. Now Arjuna should hear another, and with it he will break free from the chains of his actions.

2-40.kid: Krishna says that on this path no effort is wasted and nothing turns out wrong. Even a little of it protects a person from great fear.

2-41.kid: Krishna says a firm mind is fixed on one point. But the thoughts of people who cannot decide are endless and branch out in many directions.

2-42.kid: Krishna says unwise people speak flowery words. They delight in the words of the Vedas and say there is nothing else.

2-43.kid: Krishna says these people are full of desire and see heaven as their goal. They speak of many rituals for gaining pleasure and power, which lead to new births.

2-44.kid: Krishna says people who cling to pleasure and power, and whose minds are carried off by such words, cannot form a firm and steady mind.

2-45.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the Vedas deal with three qualities, and he should rise above them. He should be free of the pairs of opposites, always steady, not caring about getting and keeping things, and rooted in the Self.

2-46.kid: Krishna says that to someone who has truly known the Self, all the Vedas are as useful as a water tank is when there is a flood everywhere.

2-47.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that his part is the work itself, never its results. He should not work for the results, and he should not cling to doing nothing either.

2-48.kid: Krishna tells Dhananjaya to do his actions without attachment, staying perfectly balanced in both success and failure. Krishna explains that this evenness of mind is known as Yoga.

2-49.kid: Krishna says work done while wanting results is far lower than work done with a calm, even mind. Arjuna should hold to that even mind. Those who work for results are to be pitied.

2-50.kid: Krishna says that with this even mind, a person becomes free of both good and bad deeds, even in this life. So Arjuna should hold to it, because it is skill in action.

2-51.kid: Krishna says wise people with this even mind give up the results of their actions. Freed from the chains of birth, they go to a blessed state.

2-52.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that when his mind gets out of this tangle of confusion, he will no longer care about things he has heard or will yet hear.

2-53.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that his mind is now confused by many different words. When it becomes still, steady and fixed, he will reach the goal.

2-54.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna what marks a person whose mind is steady and whose wisdom is firm. How does such a person speak, sit and walk?

2-55.kid: Krishna says that when a person gives up all the desires of the mind and is content in the Self, by the Self, that person is called steady in wisdom.

2-56.kid: Krishna says a person whose mind is not shaken by pain, who does not chase after pleasure, and who is free from clinging, fear and anger, is a wise one with a steady mind.

2-57.kid: Krishna says a person who clings to nothing, who is not thrilled by good things or upset by bad things, has wisdom that is steady.

2-58.kid: Krishna says that like a tortoise pulling in its legs, a wise person can pull the senses back from the things around them. Then that person's wisdom is steady.

2-59.kid: Krishna says that when a person holds back from things, the things fall away, but the longing for them stays. Even the longing goes once that person has seen the Supreme.

2-60.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the restless senses can pull away the mind of even a wise person who is trying hard.

2-61.kid: Krishna says a person should control all the senses and sit steady, with Krishna as the highest goal. Someone whose senses are under control has steady wisdom.

2-62.kid: Krishna says that when a person keeps thinking about things, attachment to them grows. From attachment comes longing, and from longing comes anger.

2-63.kid: Krishna says anger leads to confusion, and confusion to a muddled memory. A muddled memory destroys good judgement, and when good judgement is gone, the person perishes.

2-64.kid: Krishna says a self-controlled person moves among things with the senses held in check, free from liking and disliking, and reaches peace.

2-65.kid: Krishna says that in that peace, all sorrow ends. The mind of a peaceful person soon becomes firm and steady.

2-66.kid: Krishna says an unsteady person has no true understanding and cannot focus. Without focus there is no peace, and without peace, how can anyone be happy?

2-67.kid: Krishna says that when the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away a person's understanding, just as the wind carries a boat away on the water.

2-68.kid: So, Krishna tells Arjuna, a person whose senses are fully held back from the things around them has steady wisdom.

2-69.kid: Krishna says that what is night for all beings is a time of waking for the self-controlled person. And when all other beings are awake, it is night for the wise one who sees.

2-70.kid: Krishna says the ocean stays full and still, though rivers keep flowing into it. A person who stays still like that while desires flow in finds peace, not one who chases desires.

2-71.kid: Krishna says a person who gives up all desires and lives free of longing and selfishness reaches peace.

2-72.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that this is the eternal state. Whoever reaches it is never confused. Whoever stays in it, even at the hour of death, reaches the Eternal.

3-1.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna a question. If Krishna thinks knowledge is better than action, why is he pushing Arjuna into this terrible action?

3-2.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that his words seem to pull two ways and confuse him. He asks Krishna to tell him, for certain, the one way to reach the highest.

3-3.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that there are two paths in this world: the path of knowledge, and the path of action.

3-4.kid: Krishna says no one becomes free of action just by not acting. And no one reaches perfection simply by giving things up.

3-5.kid: Krishna says no one can stay without acting, not even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act, and cannot help it, by the qualities born of nature.

3-6.kid: Krishna says a person who holds back his body from acting, but keeps thinking about the things his senses want, is confused. He is called a hypocrite.

3-7.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the one who controls his senses with his mind, and works with his body without attachment, is the one who stands out.

3-8.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to do the action that is his to do. Action is better than doing nothing, and without action he could not even keep his body going.

3-9.kid: Krishna says the world is bound by action, unless the action is done as a sacrifice. So he tells Arjuna to act for that sake, without attachment.

3-10.kid: Krishna says that in the beginning the Lord of creation made people together with sacrifice, and said: 'By this you will grow in number. Let this give you what you wish for.'

3-11.kid: Krishna goes on with those words: with sacrifice, care for the Shining Ones, and may they care for you. By caring for one another, you will reach the highest good.

3-12.kid: The Shining Ones, cared for by sacrifice, will give people the things they wish for. Krishna says that whoever enjoys their gifts and gives nothing back is a thief.

3-13.kid: Krishna says good people who eat what is left after the sacrifice are freed from all sins. But those who cook food only for themselves are eating sin.

3-14.kid: Krishna says living beings come from food, and food comes from rain. Rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.

3-15.kid: Krishna says action has a source, and that source comes from the Imperishable, which never passes away. So that which fills all things is always present in sacrifice.

3-16.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that a person who does not follow this turning wheel, living in sin and pleased only by the senses, lives his life in vain.

3-17.kid: Krishna says that a person who finds joy in the Self, and is satisfied and content in the Self alone, has nothing that he must do.

3-18.kid: Krishna says such a person has nothing to gain in this world from what he does, or from what he leaves undone. He does not depend on any being for anything.

3-19.kid: So Krishna tells Arjuna to always do the work that is his duty, without attachment. By acting without attachment, a person reaches the highest.

3-20.kid: Krishna says Janaka and others reached perfection through action. So Arjuna too should act, keeping the people of the world in mind.

3-21.kid: Krishna says that whatever a great person does, other people do too. The example he sets by what he does is the one people follow.

3-22.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that there is nothing in the three worlds that he must do, and nothing he still needs to gain. Yet he keeps on acting.

3-23.kid: Krishna says that if he ever stopped acting, without rest, people everywhere would follow his example in every way.

3-24.kid: Krishna says that if he did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin. He would be the cause of confusion among people, and he would destroy these beings.

3-25.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that unwise people act because they are attached to their work. The wise should act in the same way, but without attachment, caring for the world.

3-26.kid: Krishna says a wise person should not unsettle the minds of people who do not know and are attached to action. Acting well himself, he should help them keep to their work.

3-27.kid: Krishna says all actions are really done by the qualities of nature. But a person fooled by pride thinks, 'I am the doer.'

3-28.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that one who truly understands the qualities and their work knows that it is only qualities moving among qualities. So he does not become attached.

3-29.kid: Krishna says people fooled by the qualities of nature get attached to what the qualities do. Those whose knowledge is full should not unsettle those whose knowledge is not.

3-30.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to give all his actions to Krishna, keep his thoughts on the Self, let go of hope and selfishness, let the fever in his mind cool, and fight.

3-31.kid: Krishna says those who always follow this teaching of his, full of faith and without finding fault, are also set free from action.

3-32.kid: Krishna says those who find fault with his teaching and do not live by it are confused in all they know and lack good sense. They will come to ruin.

3-33.kid: Krishna says even a wise person acts according to his own nature. All beings follow their nature. What can holding back do?

3-34.kid: Krishna says liking and disliking the things of the senses come naturally to the senses. No one should fall under their power, for they stand in a person's way.

3-35.kid: Krishna says it is better to do your own duty, even poorly, than to do another's duty well. Even death while doing your own duty is better; another's duty is a thing to fear.

3-36.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna what pushes a person to sin, even when he does not want to, as if he were being forced.

3-37.kid: Krishna answers that it is desire, and it is anger, born of the quality of motion. It is never satisfied and full of sin. It is the enemy here on earth.

3-38.kid: Krishna says that as a fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an unborn baby by the covering around it, so this is covered by desire.

3-39.kid: Krishna says wisdom is covered over by this constant enemy of the wise: desire, which can never be satisfied, like a fire.

3-40.kid: Krishna says desire lives in the senses, the mind and reason. Through them it covers up wisdom and confuses the one who lives in the body.

3-41.kid: So Krishna tells Arjuna to first master his senses, and then to kill this sinful thing that destroys wisdom and knowledge.

3-42.kid: Krishna says the senses are great. The mind is greater than the senses, and reason is greater than the mind. But greater than reason is He.

3-43.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to know Him who is greater than reason, to hold the self steady by the Self, and to kill that enemy, desire, which is so hard to overcome.

4-1.kid: Krishna says he told this undying yoga to Vivasvat. Vivasvat told it to Manu, and Manu passed it on.

4-2.kid: Krishna says this was handed down from one to the next, and the royal sages knew it. But over a long time it faded from the world.

4-3.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that today he has told him this same old yoga, because Arjuna is his devotee and his friend. It is a deep secret.

4-4.kid: Arjuna asks how this can be. Krishna was born later and Vivasvat earlier, so how could Krishna have told it in the beginning?

4-5.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that both of them have passed through many births. Krishna knows them all, but Arjuna does not.

4-6.kid: Krishna says that though he is unborn, never changing, and Lord of all beings, he still comes to be born, through his own nature and his own power.

4-7.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that whenever what is right grows weak, and what is wrong rises up, then he himself comes forth.

4-8.kid: Krishna says he is born in every age to protect the good, to destroy those who do evil, and to set what is right firmly in place.

4-9.kid: Krishna says whoever truly knows his divine birth and action is not born again after leaving the body, but comes to him.

4-10.kid: Krishna says that many have reached his being by becoming free from attachment, fear, and anger. He says they did this by taking refuge in him and being purified by the fire of knowledge.

4-11.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that in whatever way people come to him, he meets them in that same way. The paths people take, on every side, are his.

4-12.kid: Krishna says people who want success in their actions worship the Shining Ones, because in this world of people, success from action comes quickly.

4-13.kid: Krishna says the four castes were made by him, divided by qualities and actions. He is their maker, yet he says he does not act and does not change.

4-14.kid: Krishna says actions do not touch him, and he does not long for what actions bring. Whoever knows him this way is not tied down by actions.

4-15.kid: Krishna says that, knowing this, people long ago who sought freedom still did their work. So Arjuna too should act, as they did in olden times.

4-16.kid: Krishna says even the wise are puzzled about what action is and what not acting is. So he will explain action to Arjuna, and knowing it will free him from evil.

4-17.kid: Krishna says one must understand action, forbidden action, and not acting. The way of action is hard to understand.

4-18.kid: Krishna says whoever sees not acting in action, and action in not acting, is wise among people. He is in harmony, even while doing every kind of action.

4-19.kid: Krishna says that when a person's work is free of desire for results, and his actions are burned up in the fire of wisdom, the wise call him a sage.

4-20.kid: Krishna says a person who lets go of clinging to the results of action, always content and leaning on nothing, is not really doing anything, even while acting.

4-21.kid: Krishna says one who hopes for nothing, with body and mind controlled, who has let go of grasping after things, does no wrong when he acts only with the body.

4-22.kid: Krishna says one who is happy with whatever comes without effort, untouched by the pairs of opposites, free of envy, and even-minded in success and failure, is not bound, though he acts.

4-23.kid: Krishna says that for one free of attachment, with his mind set on wisdom, who does his work as a sacrifice, all his action melts away.

4-24.kid: Krishna says the offering is the Eternal, the butter is the Eternal, the fire is the Eternal, and the one who offers is the Eternal. Whoever sees the Eternal in action goes to the Eternal.

4-25.kid: Krishna says some offer sacrifice to the Shining Ones. Others make their offering in the fire of the Eternal itself.

4-26.kid: Krishna says some offer hearing and the other senses into the fire of self-control. Others offer sound and the other things of the senses into the fire of the senses.

4-27.kid: Krishna says others offer all the work of the senses, and all the workings of life, as a sacrifice into the fire of self-control, lit by wisdom.

4-28.kid: Krishna says still others offer wealth, hard self-discipline and yoga as sacrifice. Others, firm in their vows, offer study and knowledge as sacrifice.

4-29.kid: Krishna says others offer the out-breath into the in-breath, and the in-breath into the out-breath. They hold back both breaths, given wholly to controlling the breath.

4-30.kid: Krishna says others, careful in what they eat, offer life-breaths into life-breaths. All these know what sacrifice is, and through sacrifice their sins are destroyed.

4-31.kid: Krishna says those who eat the life-giving remains of the sacrifice go to the changeless Eternal. This world is not for one who makes no sacrifice, much less the other world.

4-32.kid: Krishna says many kinds of sacrifice are spread out like this. He tells Arjuna that all of them are born of action, and knowing this, he will be free.

4-33.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the sacrifice of wisdom is better than offering any objects. All action, in the end, finds its fullness in wisdom.

4-34.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to learn this with humility, by asking questions, and by serving. The wise, who have seen the truth, will teach him this wisdom.

4-35.kid: Krishna says that once Arjuna knows this, he will not be confused like this again. He will see all beings in the Self, and in Krishna.

4-36.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that even if he were the most sinful of all sinners, the raft of wisdom would carry him across all sin.

4-37.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that just as a blazing fire burns wood to ashes, the fire of wisdom burns all actions to ashes.

4-38.kid: Krishna says nothing in this world makes one as pure as wisdom. One who becomes perfect in yoga finds it within himself, in good time.

4-39.kid: Krishna says a person full of faith, who masters his senses, gains wisdom. Having gained it, he goes quickly to the highest peace.

4-40.kid: Krishna says one who does not know, has no faith and keeps doubting, goes to destruction. For the doubting self there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.

4-41.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that actions do not bind one who has given up actions through yoga, who has cut away doubt with wisdom, and who stays steady in the Self.

4-42.kid: So Krishna tells Arjuna to cut the doubt in his heart, born of not knowing, with the sword of wisdom. He tells him to hold fast to yoga, and to stand up.

5-1.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that he praises giving up action, and then also doing it. Arjuna asks which of the two is better, and wants a clear answer.

5-2.kid: Krishna says giving up action and doing action both lead to the highest. But of the two, doing action is better than giving it up.

5-3.kid: Krishna says the one who neither hates nor desires should be known as one who always renounces. Free from the pairs of opposites, he is easily set free from what binds him.

5-4.kid: Krishna says it is children, not the wise, who call the path of knowledge and the path of action different. One who truly stands in one gets the fruit of both.

5-5.kid: Krishna says the place reached by those who follow knowledge is also reached by those who follow action. Whoever sees these two as one truly sees.

5-6.kid: Krishna says giving up action is hard to reach without the practice of action. A sage made steady by it quickly reaches the Eternal.

5-7.kid: Krishna says one who is made pure, in control of himself and his senses, and who sees his Self as the Self of all beings, is not touched by his actions.

5-8.kid: Krishna says one who knows the truth should think, 'I do nothing at all,' even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping and breathing.

5-9.kid: Krishna says that even while speaking, letting go, holding, and opening and closing his eyes, such a person holds that only the senses are moving among the things of the senses.

5-10.kid: Krishna says one who acts without attachment, placing all his actions in the Eternal, is not touched by sin, as a lotus leaf is not touched by water.

5-11.kid: Krishna says those on the path of action let go of attachment, and act only with body, mind, reason and senses, to make themselves pure.

5-12.kid: Krishna says the steady person who lets go of the results of action finds peace. The unsteady one, pushed by desire and attached to the results, is bound.

5-13.kid: Krishna says the one who is master of himself, giving up all actions in his mind, rests happily in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor making others act.

5-14.kid: Krishna says the Lord does not make people feel that they are the doers. He does not make their actions, nor join their actions to their results.

5-15.kid: Krishna says the Lord does not take up anyone's good or bad deeds. Wisdom is covered by not knowing, and so beings are confused.

5-16.kid: Krishna says that in those whose not knowing is destroyed by knowledge of the Self, that knowledge shines like the sun and shows the Supreme.

5-17.kid: Krishna says those whose thoughts rest in That, who are one with That and wholly given to That, go where there is no return, made clean by wisdom.

5-18.kid: Krishna says the wise look with an equal eye on a learned and humble man, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.

5-19.kid: Krishna says those whose minds stay balanced have overcome it all, even here on earth. The Eternal is balanced and without flaw, so they rest in the Eternal.

5-20.kid: Krishna says one who knows the Eternal and rests in it, with a steady mind and no confusion, is not overjoyed by pleasant things nor saddened by unpleasant ones.

5-21.kid: Krishna says one who is not attached to things outside, who finds joy in the Self, with his heart set on the Eternal, enjoys a happiness that never fades.

5-22.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that pleasures born of contact with outside things give birth to pain, for they begin and they end. The wise do not take delight in them.

5-23.kid: Krishna says one who, here on earth, before he is freed from the body, can stand up to the push of desire and anger, is steady, and is a happy person.

5-24.kid: Krishna says the one whose happiness is within and whose light is within becomes the Eternal, and reaches the highest goal.

5-25.kid: Krishna says that sages whose faults are gone, who are in control of themselves, and who care for the good of all beings, reach the highest goal.

5-26.kid: Krishna says the highest goal is close to those who are free of desire and anger, whose minds are controlled, and who know the Self.

5-27.kid: Krishna speaks of one who shuts out the outside world, rests his gaze between the eyebrows, and keeps the breath going in and out evenly within the nostrils.

5-28.kid: Krishna says the sage who keeps his senses, mind and reason controlled, seeks only freedom, and has cast away desire, fear and anger for ever, is truly free.

5-29.kid: Krishna says that one who knows him as the Lord of sacrifice and self-discipline, the great Lord of all the worlds, and the friend of all beings, finds peace.

6-1.kid: Krishna says that a person who does his duty without caring about its reward has truly given things up and has a steady mind. It is not the one who just gives up the fire and stops acting.

6-2.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that what people call giving things up is the same as this practice. No one reaches it without first giving up the plans and wishes his own mind makes.

6-3.kid: Krishna says that for someone who wants to reach this steady state, work is the way. Once he has reached it, calm and stillness become the way.

6-4.kid: Krishna says that when a person no longer clings to the things of the senses or to his actions, and gives up the plans his mind makes, he has reached deep concentration.

6-5.kid: Krishna says a person should lift himself up by his own self, and not let himself sink down. A person's own self can be his friend, and it can also be his enemy.

6-6.kid: Krishna says that for someone who has won over himself, his own self is his friend. But for someone who has not, his own self acts against him like an enemy.

6-7.kid: Krishna says that a calm person who has control over himself stays steady in the higher Self through cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.

6-8.kid: Krishna says a steady person is filled with wisdom and knowledge, does not waver, and controls his senses. To him, a lump of earth, a stone and gold are all the same.

6-9.kid: Krishna says that a person rises highest who looks equally on friends and enemies, strangers, people who take no side, relatives, and good and bad people alike.

6-10.kid: Krishna says that the one who meditates should practise all the time, alone in a quiet place, with his mind and body controlled, free from hoping and from wanting to own things.

6-11.kid: Krishna says he should set up his own firm seat in a clean place, not too high and not too low, made of cloth, an animal skin and grass, laid one over another.

6-12.kid: Krishna says that, sitting there, with his mind fixed on one point and his thoughts and senses held in check, he should practise meditation to make himself pure.

6-13.kid: Krishna says he should hold his body, head and neck straight and still, gazing at the tip of his nose and not looking around.

6-14.kid: Krishna says he should sit calm and without fear, firm in his vow, with his mind controlled, thinking of Krishna and holding him as the highest goal.

6-15.kid: Krishna says that the one who meditates, always keeping his mind steady and controlled like this, reaches the peace and highest joy that live in Krishna.

6-16.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that this practice is not for someone who eats too much or too little, or who sleeps too much or too little.

6-17.kid: Krishna says that for someone who keeps balance in eating and play, in work, and in sleeping and waking, this practice takes away pain and sorrow.

6-18.kid: Krishna says that when a controlled mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for anything, then the person is called steady.

6-19.kid: Krishna says that a person with a controlled mind, meditating on the Self, is like a lamp in a place with no wind. Its flame does not flicker.

6-20.kid: Krishna says there is a state where the mind, quieted by practice, finds rest. There a person sees the Self by the Self, and is happy in the Self.

6-21.kid: Krishna says that in this state a person finds the highest joy, which the understanding can grasp beyond the senses. Once he stands firm there, he never moves away from what is real.

6-22.kid: Krishna says that once a person reaches this state, he thinks there is no greater gain. Once he stands firm in it, he is not shaken even by great sorrow.

6-23.kid: Krishna says this state should be known as being set free from pain. It should be held on to firmly, without losing heart.

6-24.kid: Krishna says a person should fully give up all the wishes that come from imagining, and use his mind to hold back all his senses on every side.

6-25.kid: Krishna says that little by little, with patient and steady understanding, a person should become calm. With his mind resting in the Self, he should not think of anything.

6-26.kid: Krishna says that whenever the restless, unsteady mind wanders away, a person should bring it back each time and place it under the control of the Self.

6-27.kid: Krishna says the highest joy comes to the one who meditates when his mind is peaceful, his strong feelings are calmed, he is free from wrong, and he shares the nature of the Eternal.

6-28.kid: Krishna says that the one who keeps his mind steady like this, and is free from wrong, easily enjoys the endless joy of being in touch with the Eternal.

6-29.kid: Krishna says that a person whose heart is made steady sees the Self in all beings, and all beings in the Self. He sees the same everywhere.

6-30.kid: Krishna says that whoever sees him everywhere, and sees everything in him, is never separated from him, and Krishna is never separated from that person.

6-31.kid: Krishna says that whoever is set in oneness and worships him as living in all beings lives in Krishna, whatever way of life that person follows.

6-32.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the highest is the one who judges pleasure and pain everywhere the same way he would judge them for himself, seeing all things as equal.

6-33.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that this teaching is about keeping an even mind. But because the mind is so restless, he cannot see how it could last.

6-34.kid: Arjuna says to Krishna that the mind is restless, wild, strong and hard to bend. He thinks controlling it is as hard as controlling the wind.

6-35.kid: Krishna agrees that the mind is restless and hard to control. But he says it can be controlled by steady practice and by letting go of wanting things.

6-36.kid: Krishna says this practice is hard to reach for someone who cannot control himself. But a person who has self-control can reach it by trying in the right way.

6-37.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna about a person who has faith but cannot control himself, whose mind wanders away, and who fails to reach perfection. What happens to him?

6-38.kid: Arjuna asks whether such a person, fallen from both and lost on the path to the Eternal, is destroyed like a torn cloud, with nothing to hold him up.

6-39.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna to clear away this doubt completely, because no one but Krishna is able to take it away.

6-40.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that such a person is not destroyed, in this world or the next. Anyone who does good never comes to sorrow.

6-41.kid: Krishna says that a person who fell from this practice goes to the worlds of good people and lives there for endless years. Then he is born again into a pure and blessed home.

6-42.kid: Krishna says he may even be born into a family of wise people who meditate. But a birth like that is very rare in this world.

6-43.kid: Krishna says that there the person gets back what he had gained in his earlier body, and works even harder than before for perfection.

6-44.kid: Krishna says that his earlier practice carries him along, even without his trying. Even someone who only wishes to know about this practice rises above those who just perform rituals.

6-45.kid: Krishna says that the one who meditates and keeps working hard, made pure and growing perfect over many births, reaches the highest goal.

6-46.kid: Krishna says the one who meditates in this way is greater than those who live hard, simple lives, greater than the wise, and greater than people of action. So he tells Arjuna to become one.

6-47.kid: Krishna says that among all who meditate, the one who is full of faith, whose inner self rests in Krishna and who worships him, is the most steady of all.

7-1.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to listen. With his mind fixed on Krishna, practising and taking shelter in him, Arjuna will come to know Krishna fully, without any doubt.

7-2.kid: Krishna says he will explain this knowledge and wisdom completely. Once it is known, nothing more is left to know here.

7-3.kid: Krishna says that among thousands of people, hardly one tries for perfection. And among those who try, hardly one truly knows him.

7-4.kid: Krishna says that his nature is divided into eight parts: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, reason and ego.

7-5.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that this is his lower nature. He also has another, higher nature, and it is what holds up the whole universe.

7-6.kid: Krishna says these are the womb from which all beings come. He is where the whole universe comes from, and where it dissolves again.

7-7.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that there is nothing higher than him. Everything is strung on him, like a row of jewels on a string.

7-8.kid: Krishna says he is the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun, the Word of Power in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and the manhood in men.

7-9.kid: Krishna says he is the sweet smell of the earth and the brightness in fire. He is the life in all beings, and the self-discipline of those who live hard, simple lives.

7-10.kid: Krishna tells the son of Pritha to know him as the eternal seed of all beings. He says he is the intellect of the intelligent, and the splendor or heroism of the heroic.

7-11.kid: Krishna says he is the strength of the strong, free from desire and attachment. In all beings, he is the desire that does not go against what is right.

7-12.kid: Krishna says that all states of being, whether harmonious, active or lazy, come from him. He is not in them, but they are in him.

7-13.kid: Krishna says the whole world is fooled by these states made of the three qualities. So it does not know him, who is above them and lasts for ever.

7-14.kid: Krishna says this divine illusion of his, made of the qualities, is hard to get past. But those who come to him cross over it.

7-15.kid: Krishna says that people who do evil, who are fooled, and who are the lowest of people do not turn to him. Illusion has taken away their wisdom, and they follow the ways of demons.

7-16.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that four kinds of good people worship him: those who are suffering, those who seek knowledge, those who seek good things for themselves, and the wise.

7-17.kid: Krishna says that of these, the wise person is the best, always steady and devoted to the One. Krishna is very dear to the wise, and the wise one is dear to him.

7-18.kid: Krishna says all of them are noble, but he sees the wise person as his very own Self. With a steady mind, the wise one is fixed on Krishna as the highest goal.

7-19.kid: Krishna says that at the end of many births, the wise person comes to him, knowing that he is all. Such a great soul is very hard to find.

7-20.kid: Krishna says that people whose wisdom has been carried off by desires turn to other Shining Ones. They follow different practices, each led by their own nature.

7-21.kid: Krishna says that whatever form a devotee wants to worship with faith, Krishna makes that person's faith firm and steady.

7-22.kid: Krishna says that with that faith, the person worships that form and gets what he wishes for. But it is really Krishna who gives these gifts.

7-23.kid: Krishna says that the reward for those with little understanding has a limit. Those who worship the Shining Ones go to the Shining Ones, and those devoted to Krishna come to him.

7-24.kid: Krishna says that people without understanding think that he, who cannot be seen, has taken a form. They do not know his highest nature, which is beyond all and everlasting.

7-25.kid: Krishna says he is not seen by everyone, because he is covered by illusion. This confused world does not know him, the unborn one who lasts for ever.

7-26.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he knows all beings of the past, the present and the future. But no one knows him.

7-27.kid: Krishna says that all beings are fooled by pairs of opposites, which come from liking and disliking. Because of this, all beings fall into confusion.

7-28.kid: Krishna says that people who do good deeds, whose wrongdoing has come to an end, are freed from the confusion of opposites. They worship him, firm in their purpose.

7-29.kid: Krishna says that those who take shelter in him and strive to be free from death know the Eternal, all about the Self, and all about action.

7-30.kid: Krishna says that those who know him in the elements, in the Shining Ones and in sacrifice keep their minds steady, and know him even at the time of death.

8-1.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna what the Eternal is, what knowledge of the Self is, and what action is. He also asks what knowledge of the elements and of the Shining Ones means.

8-2.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna what sacrifice in this body is, and how it works. He also asks how people with self-control know Krishna at the time of death.

8-3.kid: Krishna says the Eternal is the highest, the one that cannot be destroyed. Its nature is called knowledge of the Self. What brings beings to birth is called action.

8-4.kid: Krishna says the elements are the part of things that perishes. The Shining Ones are about the life within. And sacrifice, here in the body, is about Krishna himself.

8-5.kid: Krishna says that whoever leaves the body at the time of death thinking only of him reaches the very being of Krishna. There is no doubt about this.

8-6.kid: Krishna says that whatever a person thinks of when leaving the body at the end, that is what he goes to, because his mind has always been turned to it.

8-7.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to think of him at all times, and fight. With his mind and understanding fixed on Krishna, Arjuna will surely come to him.

8-8.kid: Krishna says that someone whose mind does not wander to anything else, made steady by constant practice and meditation, goes to the highest divine Spirit.

8-9.kid: Krishna describes the one to think about: the Ancient One, who knows all and rules all, smaller than the smallest, holding up everything, with a form no one can imagine, shining like the sun beyond the darkness.

8-10.kid: Krishna says that at the time of death, a person full of devotion, with a still mind, who draws his life-breath to the point between the eyebrows, goes to the highest divine Spirit.

8-11.kid: Krishna says he will briefly describe what those who know the Veda call the Imperishable. The self-controlled, free from attachment, enter it, and people live lives of strict discipline to reach it.

8-12.kid: Krishna describes a person who closes all the gates of the senses, keeps his mind in the heart, holds his life-breath in his head, and stays fixed in concentration.

8-13.kid: Krishna says that a person who leaves the body saying the one syllable that is the Eternal, and thinking of Krishna, goes on the highest path.

8-14.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is easy to reach for the steady person who thinks of him always, every day, and never of anything else.

8-15.kid: Krishna says that great souls who have come to him are not born again. Birth is a place of pain that does not last. They have reached the highest joy.

8-16.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that all the worlds come and go. But a person who comes to Krishna is not born again.

8-17.kid: Krishna says that people who know of the great day that lasts a thousand ages, and the night that lasts a thousand ages, truly know what day and night are.

8-18.kid: Krishna says that when that day comes, all things that can be seen come out of the unseen. When night comes, they melt back into the unseen.

8-19.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the same crowd of beings is born again and again. When night comes it melts away, not by its own choice, and when day comes it appears again.

8-20.kid: Krishna says that beyond this unseen state there is another unseen one that is eternal. When all beings are destroyed, it is not destroyed.

8-21.kid: Krishna says this unseen one is called the Imperishable and the highest goal. Those who reach it do not come back. It is his own highest home.

8-22.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the highest Spirit, in whom all beings live and who fills everything, can be reached by whole-hearted devotion to him alone.

8-23.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he will now explain the times when those who meditate leave and do not return, and when they leave and do return.

8-24.kid: Krishna says that those who know the Eternal, and leave in fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight and the six months of the northern path, go to the Eternal.

8-25.kid: Krishna says that the one who meditates and leaves in smoke, night-time, the dark fortnight and the six months of the southern path reaches the light of the moon, and returns.

8-26.kid: Krishna says the light path and the dark path are thought to be the world's everlasting paths. By one, a person does not return. By the other, he returns again.

8-27.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that one who knows these paths is never confused. So Arjuna should stay steady in this practice at all times.

8-28.kid: Krishna says the one who knows this goes beyond all the good rewards of the Vedas, of sacrifices, of self-discipline and of giving gifts, and reaches the highest, most ancient home.

9-1.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna, who does not find fault, that he will now share the deepest secret knowledge. When Arjuna knows it, he will be set free from evil.

9-2.kid: Krishna says this knowledge is the highest, the deepest secret and the greatest purifier. It can be known directly, it is good, it is very easy to practise, and it never perishes.

9-3.kid: Krishna says that people who have no faith in this teaching do not reach him. They come back again to the path of this world, a world of death.

9-4.kid: Krishna says that, in a form that cannot be seen, he fills this whole world. All beings rest in him, but he does not rest in them.

9-5.kid: Then Krishna says that beings do not really rest in him either, and asks Arjuna to see his wonderful power. He brings beings forth and holds them up, yet he does not dwell in them.

9-6.kid: Krishna gives a picture. The mighty wind moves everywhere, yet it always rests in space. In the same way, he says, all beings rest in him.

9-7.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that at the end of an age of the world, all beings go back into his nature. When a new age begins, he sends them out again.

9-8.kid: Krishna says that through his own nature he brings forth all these many beings, again and again. They are helpless, carried along by the power of that nature.

9-9.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that these works do not bind him. He sits apart from them, like one who takes no side, not attached to what he does.

9-10.kid: Krishna says that with him near, watching over it, nature brings forth everything that moves and everything that does not. Because of this, the world keeps turning.

9-11.kid: Krishna says that foolish people look down on him when he comes in a human body. They do not know his higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.

9-12.kid: Krishna says such people have empty hopes, empty deeds and empty knowledge. They have lost their good sense and take on a cruel, deceiving, demon-like nature.

9-13.kid: Krishna says the great-souled ones share his divine nature. They know him as the never-ending source of all beings, and they worship him with a mind that never wavers.

9-14.kid: Krishna says these people are always praising him and trying hard, firm in what they have promised. They bow down to him with devotion and worship him, always steady.

9-15.kid: Krishna says that others worship him by offering wisdom. They see him as the One and as the many, present everywhere.

9-16.kid: Krishna says that he is every part of the holy offering: the rite, the offering to the ancestors, the herb, the sacred words, the butter, the fire and the offering itself.

9-17.kid: Krishna says he is the father and the mother of this world, its supporter and its grandfather. He is the holy one to be known, the sacred word, and the old sacred hymns.

9-18.kid: Krishna goes on. He is the way and the goal, the lord, the witness, the home, the shelter, the dear one, the beginning and the ending, the ground, the storehouse, and the seed that never dies.

9-19.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he gives heat, and he holds back and sends forth the rain. He is deathlessness and also death. He is what is and what is not.

9-20.kid: Krishna says some who know the three Vedas worship him with offerings, are made clean of wrong, and pray to reach heaven. They reach the holy world of the ruler of the Shining Ones and enjoy its divine joys.

9-21.kid: Krishna says that when they have enjoyed the wide heaven-world and their goodness is used up, they come back to this world of death. Because they want what they desire, they keep coming and going.

9-22.kid: Krishna says that he takes full care of those who worship him alone, thinking of nothing apart from him, and who stay always steady.

9-23.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that people who worship other Shining Ones with faith are worshipping him too, even though they do not follow the old rule.

9-24.kid: Krishna says that he is the one who receives every offering, and he is its Lord. But these people do not truly know him, and so they fall back.

9-25.kid: Krishna says that those who worship the Shining Ones go to them, those who worship the ancestors go to the ancestors, and those who offer to the elements go to the elements. Those who worship him come to him.

9-26.kid: Krishna says that if someone offers him a leaf, a flower, a fruit or some water with devotion, he accepts that gift, given with devotion.

9-27.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that whatever he does, whatever he eats, whatever he offers, whatever he gives away and whatever hard practice he keeps, he should do it all as an offering to Krishna.

9-28.kid: Krishna says that in this way Arjuna will be freed from the bonds of action, with their good and bad results. His heart steady in letting go, he will be free and come to Krishna.

9-29.kid: Krishna says he is the same to all beings. He hates no one, and no one is his favourite. But those who worship him with devotion are in him, and he is in them.

9-30.kid: Krishna says that even if a very wicked person worships him with a whole heart, turning to no one else, that person should be thought of as good, because they have chosen rightly.

9-31.kid: Krishna says such a person soon becomes good and reaches lasting peace. He tells Arjuna to know for certain that one who is devoted to him is never destroyed.

9-32.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that those who take shelter in him reach the highest goal too, whatever birth they come from.

9-33.kid: Krishna says this is even more true of holy people and devoted royal sages. He tells Arjuna that, having come into this passing and joyless world, he should worship Krishna.

9-34.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to fill his mind with him, be devoted to him, offer to him and bow to him. With his heart steady like this, and Krishna as his highest goal, he will come to Krishna.

10-1.kid: Krishna asks mighty Arjuna to listen once more to his highest word. He will tell it because he wishes Arjuna well.

10-2.kid: Krishna says that neither the crowds of Shining Ones nor the great sages know where he comes from, because he is the beginning of them all.

10-3.kid: Krishna says that whoever knows him as never born, without beginning, the great Lord of the world, is not confused. Among all people, that one is freed from every wrong.

10-4.kid: Krishna begins a list of the qualities of living beings: understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-control, calm, happiness and pain, coming to be and ceasing to be, fear and courage.

10-5.kid: He finishes the list: not harming, evenness, contentment, self-discipline, giving, a good name and a bad name. Krishna says all these different qualities of beings come from him.

10-6.kid: Krishna says that the seven great sages of old, and the Manus, were born from his mind. All the creatures in the world came from them.

10-7.kid: Krishna says that whoever truly knows his greatness and his power becomes steady in a way that never wavers. There is no doubt about it.

10-8.kid: Krishna says he is the source of everything, and everything grows from him. The wise know this, and they worship him with deep and loving hearts.

10-9.kid: Krishna says the wise keep their minds on him and their lives in him. They help each other understand, always talk about him, and are happy and content.

10-10.kid: Krishna says that to these people, who are always steady and worship him with love, he gives the gift of clear understanding, by which they come to him.

10-11.kid: Krishna says that out of pure kindness he lives in their hearts. With the shining lamp of wisdom, he destroys the darkness that comes from not knowing.

10-12.kid: Arjuna praises Krishna. He calls Krishna the highest, the highest home and the highest purity, eternal and divine, the very first, never born, and the Lord.

10-13.kid: Arjuna says that all the great sages have spoken of Krishna this way, and so have Asita and Devala and others. Now Krishna tells him the same thing himself.

10-14.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that he believes everything Krishna says is true. He says that not even the Shining Ones, nor other mighty beings, understand how Krishna shows himself.

10-15.kid: Arjuna says that only Krishna knows himself, by himself. He calls Krishna the source of beings, the Lord of beings, the Shining One of Shining Ones and the ruler of the world.

10-16.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna to tell him fully about his divine glories, the glories by which Krishna fills all these worlds and remains in them.

10-17.kid: Arjuna asks how he can come to know Krishna by thinking of him always. In which things, he asks, should he think of Krishna?

10-18.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna to tell him again, in detail, about his power and glory. He says he can never hear enough of the life-giving words Krishna speaks.

10-19.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna, the best of the Kurus, that he will name only the chief of his divine glories, because there is no end to the details.

10-20.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is the Self living in the heart of every being. He is the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.

10-21.kid: Krishna says that among the Adityas he is Vishnu, and among lights he is the bright sun. He is Marichi among the winds, and the Moon among the stars.

10-22.kid: Krishna says that among the Vedas he is one special Veda, and among the gods he is Indra. Of the senses he is the mind, and in living beings he is understanding.

10-23.kid: Krishna says that of the Rudras he is Sankara, and of the Yakshas he is Kuvera, the lord of wealth. He is Meru among the high mountains.

10-24.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that of priests he is the chief, Brihaspati. He is Skanda among army leaders, and the ocean among all the waters.

10-25.kid: Krishna says that of the great sages he is Bhrigu, and of words he is the one syllable. He is quiet, repeated prayer among offerings, and the mighty mountains among things that never move.

10-26.kid: Krishna says that of all trees he is the Asvattha. He is Chitraratha among the Gandharvas, and the sage Kapila among the perfected ones.

10-27.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to know him as Uchchaishravas among horses, born from nectar. He is one special elephant among the lordly elephants, and the king among men.

10-28.kid: Krishna says that of weapons he is the thunderbolt, and he is Kandarpa, who brings children into being. He is also one special cow, and one special serpent.

10-29.kid: Krishna says that of snakes he is Ananta, of the beings of the water he is Varuna, of the ancestors he is Aryaman, and of those who rule and control he is Yama.

10-30.kid: Krishna says that among the Daityas he is Prahlada, and of all that measures he is Time. Among wild beasts he is the lord of beasts, and among birds he is Garuda.

10-31.kid: Krishna says that of things that make clean he is the wind, and of warriors he is Rama. He is the shark among fishes, and the Ganges among rivers.

10-32.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is the beginning, the middle and the end of all that is made. Of all knowledge he is knowing the Self, and he is the speech of those who debate.

10-33.kid: Krishna says that of letters he is the letter A, and of joined words he is the pair. He is endless Time, and the one who holds up all, facing every way.

10-34.kid: Krishna says he is all-devouring Death and the origin of all to come. Of feminine qualities, he is fame, prosperity, speech or inspiration, memory, intelligence, constancy, and forgiveness.

10-35.kid: Krishna says that of hymns he is the Brihatsaman, and of meters he is the Gayatri. Of months he is Margasirsha, and of seasons he is the flowery season.

10-36.kid: Krishna says he is the gambling of the cheat, and the greatness of the great. He is victory, he is firm effort, and he is the goodness of the good.

10-37.kid: Krishna says that among the Vrishnis he is Vasudeva, and among the Pandavas he is Dhananjaya. Of the sages he is Vyasa, and of the poets he is Ushanas.

10-38.kid: Krishna says that of rulers he is the sceptre, and of those who seek to win he is wise leadership. He is silence among secrets, and the knowledge of those who know.

10-39.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is the seed of all beings. Nothing at all, moving or still, can exist without him.

10-40.kid: Krishna says there is no end to his divine powers. What he has told is only a small part, a few examples of his endless glory.

10-41.kid: Krishna says that whatever is glorious and mighty comes from just a small part of his splendour.

10-42.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna what use all these details are to him. Krishna fills and holds up this whole universe with just one small part of himself, and he remains.

11-1.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that the deep words about the Self, which Krishna spoke out of kindness, have taken away his confusion.

11-2.kid: Arjuna says that he has heard from Krishna, in detail, how beings begin and end, and about the greatness of Krishna that never ends.

11-3.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that all he has said about himself is true. Still, Arjuna wants to see his all-powerful form as the supreme Lord.

11-4.kid: Arjuna says that if Krishna thinks he is able to see it, then Krishna should show him his Self that never perishes.

11-5.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to look and see his forms, by hundreds and thousands. They are divine, and of many kinds, colours and shapes.

11-6.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to look at the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and the Maruts, and at many wonders never seen before.

11-7.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that here, today, he can see the whole universe, moving and still, gathered as one in the body of Krishna, along with anything else he wants to see.

11-8.kid: Krishna says that Arjuna cannot see him with his own eyes. So Krishna gives him a divine eye, and tells him to look at his great power.

11-9.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that after saying this, Hari, the great Lord, showed Arjuna his highest form as Lord.

11-10.kid: Sanjaya describes the form. It has many mouths and eyes, many wonderful sights, many divine ornaments, and many divine weapons held up high.

11-11.kid: Sanjaya says the form wore divine garlands and clothes, and was covered in heavenly sweet-smelling oils. It was full of wonders, without limits, and faced every way.

11-12.kid: Sanjaya says that if the light of a thousand suns blazed out in the sky all at once, it might be like the glory of that mighty being.

11-13.kid: Sanjaya says that there, in the body of the God of gods, Arjuna saw the whole universe, with all its many parts, gathered together as one.

11-14.kid: Sanjaya says Arjuna was filled with wonder, and his hair stood on end. He bowed his head to the Shining One, joined his palms, and spoke.

11-15.kid: Arjuna says that in the form of Krishna he sees all the gods and all kinds of beings, Brahma the Lord seated on the lotus, all the sages, and the divine serpents.

11-16.kid: Arjuna says he sees Krishna everywhere, without limits, with countless arms, mouths and eyes. He sees no end, no middle and no beginning to him.

11-17.kid: Arjuna sees him with a crown, a mace and a discus. He is a mass of light shining everywhere, blazing like fire and the sun, hard to look at, and too vast to measure.

11-18.kid: Arjuna tells Krishna that he is the highest, the one who never perishes. He is the undying guardian of what is eternally right, and the most ancient being.

11-19.kid: Arjuna sees him without beginning, middle or end, with endless power and many arms. The sun and moon are his eyes, his mouth is a blazing fire, and his brightness heats the whole universe.

11-20.kid: Arjuna says Krishna alone fills the earth, the heavens and all the space between. When they see his wondrous and fearsome form, the three worlds tremble.

11-21.kid: Arjuna sees crowds of gods entering into Krishna. Some praise him in fear with joined palms. Bands of great sages and perfected ones call out blessings and sing his praises.

11-22.kid: Arjuna names many groups of beings, among them the Rudras, Vasus, Ashvins, Maruts, Gandharvas and Yakshas. All of them are looking at Krishna, amazed.

11-23.kid: Arjuna says that when they see the huge form of Krishna, with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs and feet, and many fearful teeth, the worlds are terrified, and so is he.

11-24.kid: Arjuna sees Krishna touching the sky, shining in many colours, with mouths wide open and huge fiery eyes. His heart shakes with fear, and he has lost his courage and his peace.

11-25.kid: Arjuna sees the mouths of Krishna, with fearful teeth, blazing like fires that destroy. He feels lost and can find no peace, and he begs Krishna for mercy.

11-26.kid: Arjuna sees the sons of Dhritarashtra with many kings, and Bhishma and Drona, and the best warriors of his own side too, all rushing into the terrible mouths of Krishna.

11-27.kid: Arjuna sees them rushing into the gaping mouths of Krishna, with their terrible teeth. Some are caught between the teeth, their heads crushed to powder.

11-28.kid: Arjuna says that just as many rivers rush to the ocean, these mighty heroes of the world rush into the flaming mouths of Krishna.

11-29.kid: Arjuna says that just as moths fly fast into a blazing fire and die, these people rush quickly into the mouths of Krishna and perish.

11-30.kid: Arjuna sees Krishna swallowing everything on every side with flaming mouths. His fierce rays fill the whole world with light, and they are burning.

11-31.kid: Arjuna asks who Krishna is in this fierce form. He bows to him and begs for mercy. He wants to know Krishna truly, because he does not understand what he sees.

11-32.kid: Krishna says he is mighty Time, which destroys the world, and he has shown himself here. None of the warriors lined up in the armies will live.

11-33.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to stand up and win fame, defeat his enemies and enjoy the kingdom. Krishna says they are already overcome by him, and Arjuna is only the outward cause.

11-34.kid: Krishna names Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and other brave warriors. He says they are already slain by him, and tells Arjuna to kill them without fear, fight, and win the battle.

11-35.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that when Arjuna heard these words, he joined his palms, trembling, and bowed low. He was full of fear, and he spoke again to Krishna in a shaking voice.

11-36.kid: Arjuna says it is right that the world rejoices and sings the praise of Krishna. Some beings run in fear to every side, and the hosts of Siddhas bow down to him.

11-37.kid: Arjuna asks how they could not bow to Krishna, the first cause, greater than all. He is endless, the God of gods, the home of the worlds, the undying, being and not-being, and what is beyond.

11-38.kid: Arjuna says that Krishna is the first of the gods and the most ancient being. He is the highest resting place of all, the knower and the known, and the whole universe is spread out in him.

11-39.kid: Arjuna says Krishna is Yama, Agni, Varuna and the moon, the forefather of all. He bows to him in greeting a thousand times, and again and again.

11-40.kid: Arjuna bows to Krishna in front, behind and on every side. Krishna has endless power and strength, and he fills everything, so he is everything.

11-41.kid: Arjuna remembers how he called out to Krishna as just a friend, saying "O Krishna, O friend," not knowing his greatness, careless because of his love.

11-42.kid: Arjuna says that if he ever joked with Krishna without respect, at play, resting, sitting or eating, alone or with others, he asks Krishna, the boundless one, to forgive him.

11-43.kid: Arjuna says Krishna is the father of the world, of all that moves and all that stands still. No one in the worlds is equal to him, so who could be greater?

11-44.kid: Arjuna bows down and asks Krishna to bear with him and forgive him, as a father forgives a son, a friend a friend, and one who loves the one they love.

11-45.kid: Arjuna is glad to have seen what he had never seen before, yet his mind is full of fear. He asks Krishna to have mercy and show his other form again.

11-46.kid: Arjuna wants to see Krishna as before, wearing a crown and holding a mace and a discus. He asks the thousand-armed one to take on his four-armed form again.

11-47.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that by his own kindness and power he has shown him this highest form. It is shining, endless and first of all, and no one but Arjuna has ever seen it.

11-48.kid: Krishna says that no offerings, study of the Vedas, gifts, rituals or hard practices can win this vision for anyone in the world of men. Only Arjuna has seen it.

11-49.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna not to be afraid or confused at seeing this fearsome form. He should let go of fear, be glad at heart, and see his familiar form again.

11-50.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that after speaking, Krishna showed Arjuna his own form again. He took a gentle form once more and comforted Arjuna, who was frightened.

11-51.kid: Arjuna says that now he sees the gentle human form of Krishna again, his mind is calm and he feels like himself once more.

11-52.kid: Krishna says this form of his that Arjuna has seen is very hard to see. Even the Shining Ones always long to see it.

11-53.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he cannot be seen as Arjuna has seen him through the Vedas, hard practices, gifts or offerings.

11-54.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that only by devotion to him alone can he be known like this, truly seen, and entered into.

11-55.kid: Krishna says that whoever works for him, has him as their goal, is devoted to him, is free from clinging and hates no living being, comes to him.

12-1.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna a question. Some faithful people always worship Krishna himself, steady in heart. Others worship the unseen one that never perishes. Which of them knows the way better?

12-2.kid: Krishna answers. Those who fix their minds on him, worship him steadily and have the greatest faith are, in his view, the ones who know the way best.

12-3.kid: Krishna speaks of people who worship the one that never perishes. It cannot be described or seen, or even thought about. It is everywhere, never changes, never moves, and lasts forever.

12-4.kid: Krishna says these people also come to him, when they control their senses, treat everything equally, and give themselves to the good of all beings.

12-5.kid: Krishna says the way is harder for those whose minds are set on the unseen. For anyone living in a body, that goal is very hard to reach.

12-6.kid: Krishna speaks of those who give all their actions over to him. They keep him as their goal, and worship him by thinking of him with their whole heart.

12-7.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he soon lifts these people out of the ocean of life and death, because their minds are fixed on him.

12-8.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to fix his mind on him and give him his understanding too. Then, without doubt, Arjuna will live in Krishna afterwards.

12-9.kid: Krishna says that if Arjuna cannot keep his mind steady on him, he should try to reach him through practice.

12-10.kid: Krishna says that if Arjuna cannot keep up steady practice, he should do his actions for the sake of Krishna. Even by doing that, he will reach perfection.

12-11.kid: Krishna says that if even this is too hard, Arjuna should take shelter in him, control himself, and give up the fruit of all his actions.

12-12.kid: Krishna says knowledge is better than practice alone. Meditation is better than knowledge. Better than meditation is giving up the fruit of actions, and peace follows giving it up.

12-13.kid: Krishna describes a person who hates no creature. He is friendly and kind to all, free from thinking only of "I" and "mine", calm in pain and pleasure, and forgiving.

12-14.kid: Such a person is always content, steady, self-controlled and firm, with mind and understanding given to Krishna. Krishna says this devoted person is dear to him.

12-15.kid: Krishna says a person who does not upset the world, and is not upset by it, is dear to him. Such a person is not carried away by joy, fear or worry.

12-16.kid: Krishna says the devoted person who is dear to him depends on nothing and wants nothing. He is pure, quick to act, calm and untroubled, and gives up every new plan.

12-17.kid: Krishna says a person who is not carried away by gladness or hate, grief or longing, who gives up both good and evil, and is full of devotion, is dear to him.

12-18.kid: Krishna describes a person who is the same to friend and enemy, the same in honour and shame, in cold and heat, and in pleasure and pain. He clings to nothing.

12-19.kid: He takes praise and blame alike. He is quiet, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady in mind and full of devotion. Krishna says such a person is dear to him.

12-20.kid: Krishna says those who follow the teaching he has just given, with faith, making him their highest goal and devoted to him, are especially dear to him.

13-1.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that this body is called the Field. Those who know call the one who knows it the Knower of the Field.

13-2.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to know that he is the Knower of the Field in every field. To Krishna, knowing the Field and its Knower is the real knowledge.

13-3.kid: Krishna says he will briefly explain what the Field is, what it is like, how it changes and where it comes from, and also who knows it and what powers he has.

13-4.kid: Krishna says wise sages have sung of this in many ways, in many different chants, and in verses full of careful reasoning.

13-5.kid: Krishna lists what makes up the field: the great elements, the sense of self, the power to understand, the unseen, the ten senses and the mind, and the five things the senses meet.

13-6.kid: Krishna goes on: desire and dislike, pleasure and pain, combination, intelligence and firmness. In short, he says, this is the Field with its changes.

13-7.kid: Krishna begins a list: being humble, not showing off, not harming anyone, forgiving others, being upright, serving the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control.

13-8.kid: The list goes on: letting go of the things the senses want, not being full of oneself, and thinking about the pain and evil of birth, death, old age and sickness.

13-9.kid: The list goes on: not clinging, not mistaking son, wife or home for oneself, and always staying calm whether wanted or unwanted things happen.

13-10.kid: Krishna goes on: steady devotion to him that never turns aside, going to quiet places apart, and not seeking the company of other people.
