13-11.kid: Krishna ends the list: always holding to knowledge of the Self, and understanding what true knowledge is for. All this is called wisdom, and whatever goes against it is ignorance.

13-12.kid: Krishna says he will now describe what must be known. By knowing it, a person gains immortality. It is the highest, it has no beginning, and it is called neither being nor non-being.

13-13.kid: Krishna says That has hands and feet everywhere. It has eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, and hears everywhere. It lives in the world, wrapping around everything.

13-14.kid: Krishna says That shines through all the senses, yet has no senses. It clings to nothing, yet holds everything up. It is free from the qualities, yet it experiences them.

13-15.kid: Krishna says That is outside and inside all beings. It is both still and moving. It is so fine it cannot be grasped. It is far away, and also near.

13-16.kid: Krishna says That is not divided, yet it seems to be divided among beings. It holds beings up. It both swallows them up and brings them forth.

13-17.kid: Krishna says That is the light of all lights, beyond darkness. It is knowledge, what is to be known, and what knowledge reaches. It lives in the hearts of all.

13-18.kid: Krishna says he has now briefly explained the Field, knowledge, and what is to be known. His devotee who understands this is able to come to his own being.

13-19.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that matter and spirit both have no beginning. All changes and all qualities, he says, are born from matter.

13-20.kid: Krishna says matter is called the cause of things being produced. Spirit is called the cause of feeling pleasure and pain.

13-21.kid: Krishna says spirit, living in matter, experiences the qualities born of matter. It is clinging to those qualities that makes it born into good and evil wombs.

13-22.kid: Krishna says the highest spirit in this body has many names: the one who watches, the one who allows, the supporter, the one who experiences, the great Lord and the highest Self.

13-23.kid: Krishna says whoever truly knows spirit and matter, with its qualities, is not born again, whatever kind of life he lives.

13-24.kid: Krishna says some people see the Self within through meditation. Others see it by the path of knowledge, and others by the path of action.

13-25.kid: Krishna says others do not know this, but they worship as they have heard from others. They hold fast to what they heard, and they too go beyond death.

13-26.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that every creature that is born, whether it moves or stays still, comes from the joining of the Field and the Knower of the Field.

13-27.kid: Krishna says the one who truly sees is the one who sees the highest Lord living equally in all beings, never dying within all that dies.

13-28.kid: Krishna says a person who sees the same Lord living equally everywhere does not harm the Self, and so he reaches the highest goal.

13-29.kid: Krishna says the one who truly sees understands that matter does all actions, and that the Self does not act at all.

13-30.kid: Krishna says that when a person sees all the many different beings as rooted in the One, and spreading out from it, then he reaches the Eternal.

13-31.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the highest Self has no beginning and no qualities, and never perishes. Even while living in the body, it does not act and nothing touches it.

13-32.kid: Krishna says the open space that is everywhere is so fine that nothing touches it. In the same way, the Self that is everywhere in the body is untouched.

13-33.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that just as the one sun lights up the whole world, the Lord of the Field lights up the whole Field.

13-34.kid: Krishna says those who see with the eye of wisdom the difference between the Field and its Knower, and how beings are set free from matter, go to the Supreme.

14-1.kid: Krishna says he will again share the highest wisdom, the best of all wisdom. By knowing it, all the sages reached the highest perfection after this life.

14-2.kid: Krishna says those who hold to this wisdom and come to his own nature are not born again when a universe begins, and are not troubled when it ends.

14-3.kid: Krishna tells the descendant of Bharata that his womb is the great Eternal or Prakriti. He places the germ inside it, and from there all beings are born.

14-4.kid: Krishna tells the son of Kunti that whatever forms are produced in all wombs, the great Eternal or Prakriti is their true womb, and he is the seed-giving father.

14-5.kid: Krishna names the qualities born of matter: harmony, motion and inertia. He tells Arjuna that they bind the undying one who lives in the body, holding it fast there.

14-6.kid: Krishna says harmony is spotless and full of light. It binds a person too, by making them cling to happiness and to knowledge.

14-7.kid: Krishna says motion is full of passion and causes craving and clinging. It binds the one who lives in the body by making it cling to action.

14-8.kid: Krishna says inertia is born of ignorance and confuses everyone who lives in a body. It binds them through confusion, laziness and sleepiness.

14-9.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that harmony ties a person to happiness, and motion ties a person to action. Inertia covers up clear understanding and ties a person to confusion.

14-10.kid: Krishna says that at times harmony wins over motion and inertia. At times motion wins over harmony and inertia. And at times inertia wins over harmony and motion.

14-11.kid: Krishna says that when the light of wisdom shines out through every sense of the body, then it can be known that harmony is growing strong.

14-12.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that greed, busy activity, starting new actions, restlessness and longing all arise when motion grows strong.

14-13.kid: Krishna says darkness, dullness, confusion and being misled all arise when inertia grows strong.

14-14.kid: Krishna says that if a person dies while harmony is strong in him, he goes on to the spotless worlds.

14-15.kid: Krishna says that if a person dies while motion is strong, he is born among those attached to action. If he dies in inertia, he is born in the wombs of those without reason.

14-16.kid: Krishna says the fruit of good action is said to be pure. The fruit of motion is pain, and the fruit of inertia is ignorance.

14-17.kid: Krishna says wisdom comes from harmony, and greed comes from motion. And confusion, being misled and ignorance come from inertia.

14-18.kid: Krishna says those settled in harmony rise upward. Those in motion stay in the middle. Those in inertia, held by the lowest quality, go downward.

14-19.kid: Krishna says that when a seer sees no doer other than the qualities, and knows what is higher than the qualities, he comes to the very being of Krishna.

14-20.kid: Krishna says that when the one in the body goes beyond these three qualities, from which bodies come, he is freed from birth, death, old age and sorrow, and becomes immortal.

14-21.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna how to tell a person who has gone beyond the three qualities. How does such a person act, and how does he get beyond them?

14-22.kid: Krishna answers Arjuna. Such a person does not hate light, activity or delusion when they come, and does not long for them when they are gone.

14-23.kid: Krishna says such a person sits as if unconcerned and is not shaken by the qualities. Knowing that the qualities are at work, he stays steady and does not move.

14-24.kid: Krishna says such a person is even in pleasure and pain, settled in himself, and sees a lump of earth, a stone and gold as alike. He is firm, and the same to liked and disliked, blame and praise.

14-25.kid: Krishna says such a person is the same in honour and shame, the same to friend and enemy, and gives up all his projects. He is said to have gone beyond the qualities.

14-26.kid: Krishna says whoever serves him with devotion that never wavers goes beyond the qualities and becomes fit to become the Eternal.

14-27.kid: Krishna says he is the home of the Eternal, of what is deathless and unchanging, of the right way that lasts forever, and of endless bliss.

15-1.kid: Krishna speaks of a tree that is said to last forever, with its roots above and its branches below. Its leaves are hymns. Whoever knows this tree knows the Vedas.

15-2.kid: Krishna says the tree's branches spread up and down, fed by the qualities, with the things of the senses as its buds. Its roots stretch down into the world of people, bound up with action.

15-3.kid: Krishna says no one here can see the tree's true form, its end, its beginning or what it stands on. It is firmly rooted, but it can be cut down with the strong weapon of not clinging.

15-4.kid: Then, Krishna says, one should seek the path from which there is no coming back, and turn to that ancient, original one from whom all activity streamed out.

15-5.kid: Krishna says those free of pride and delusion, who have beaten clinging, always rest in the Self, have quieted their desires and are free of pleasure and pain as opposites, reach that undying goal.

15-6.kid: Krishna says neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire lights up that place. Those who go there do not return. That is his highest home.

15-7.kid: Krishna says a part of his own self becomes an undying living soul in the world of life. Living in matter, it draws to itself the senses, with the mind as the sixth.

15-8.kid: Krishna says that when the Lord takes a body and when he leaves it, he takes the senses with him, the way the wind carries off sweet smells.

15-9.kid: Krishna says the Lord lives in the ear, the eye, touch, taste and smell, and in the mind too. He enjoys the things of the senses through them.

15-10.kid: Krishna says confused people do not see the Lord as he leaves a body, stays in it, or enjoys things through the qualities. Those with the eye of wisdom see him.

15-11.kid: Krishna says seekers who strive see him living within themselves. But those who are untrained and unwise do not see him, even though they try.

15-12.kid: Krishna says the light of the sun that lights up the whole world, and the light in the moon and in fire, all comes from him.

15-13.kid: Krishna says he enters the earth and holds up all beings with his energy, and he nourishes all the plants.

15-14.kid: Krishna says he becomes the fire of life inside the bodies of living things. He joins with their breath and digests the four kinds of food.

15-15.kid: Krishna says he lives in the hearts of all. Memory and wisdom, and losing them, come from him. He is what all the Vedas teach, he knows the Vedas, and he is the author of the Vedanta.

15-16.kid: Krishna says there are two kinds in this world: one that perishes and one that does not. All beings perish. The unchanging one is called the one that does not perish.

15-17.kid: Krishna says there is yet another, the highest, called the Supreme Self. He fills the three worlds, holds them up, and is the Lord who never perishes.

15-18.kid: Krishna says he is beyond what perishes and higher even than what does not. So in the world and in the Veda he is known as the highest Spirit.

15-19.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that whoever is free of confusion and knows him as the highest Spirit knows everything, and worships him with his whole heart.

15-20.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna he has now shared this deepest, most secret teaching. Whoever understands it becomes truly wise and has done all his work.

16-1.kid: Krishna begins a list: fearlessness, a pure heart, steadiness in wisdom, giving to others, self-control, sacrifice, study of the scriptures, strict discipline and being straightforward.

16-2.kid: The list goes on: not harming, truth, no anger, letting go, peace, kindness to all beings, not being greedy, gentleness, modesty and steadiness.

16-3.kid: Krishna ends the list: courage, forgiveness, strength to endure, purity, no ill will and no pride. He tells Arjuna these belong to a person born with a divine nature.

16-4.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that putting on a show, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to a person born with a demon-like nature.

16-5.kid: Krishna says the divine nature leads to freedom, and the demon-like nature leads to being bound. He tells Arjuna not to grieve, because Arjuna was born with the divine nature.

16-6.kid: Krishna says there are two kinds of beings in this world, the divine and the demon-like. He has described the divine at length, and now he tells Arjuna about the demon-like.

16-7.kid: Krishna says people of demon-like nature do not know what to do and what not to do. There is no purity, no good conduct and no truth in them.

16-8.kid: Krishna says such people claim the universe has no truth, no basis and no God. They say it came about by things joining together, caused only by desire.

16-9.kid: Krishna says that, holding this view, these ruined souls of small understanding and fierce deeds rise up as enemies of the world, to destroy it.

16-10.kid: Krishna says such people give in to desires that are never satisfied. Full of pride and arrogance, holding wrong ideas because they are confused, they act with impure aims.

16-11.kid: Krishna says they are caught up in endless worries that end only in death. They think satisfying their desires is the highest thing, and feel sure that this is all.

16-12.kid: Krishna says they are tied by a hundred hopes and given over to desire and anger. They try to pile up wealth by unfair means, for their own pleasure.

16-13.kid: Krishna describes how such a person thinks: 'I got this today. I will get that wish too. This is mine already, and that wealth will be mine later.'

16-14.kid: Krishna says such a person also thinks: 'I have killed that enemy, and I will kill others too. I am the lord. I enjoy. I am powerful and happy.'

16-15.kid: Such a person thinks: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is like me? I will make sacrifices, give gifts and enjoy myself.' Krishna says they are fooled by ignorance.

16-16.kid: Krishna says that, confused by many thoughts, caught in a net of delusion and hooked on getting what they desire, they fall down into a foul hell.

16-17.kid: Krishna says these proud, stubborn people, full of the pride of wealth, offer sacrifices only in name, to show off, ignoring the rules.

16-18.kid: Krishna says that, full of selfishness, power, rudeness, desire and anger, these spiteful people hate him, in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.

16-19.kid: Krishna says he keeps casting these hateful, cruel people, the lowest of people, into demon-like births.

16-20.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that, born into demon-like births and confused birth after birth, they do not reach him, and they sink lower and lower.

16-21.kid: Krishna says there are three gates to this hell, which ruin the self: desire, anger and greed. So a person should give up these three.

16-22.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that a person who gets free of these three gates of darkness does what is good for himself, and so reaches the highest goal.

16-23.kid: Krishna says a person who sets aside what the scriptures teach and just follows his desires does not reach perfection, or happiness, or the highest goal.

16-24.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to let the scriptures guide him in deciding what to do and what not to do. Knowing what they teach, he should act in this world.

17-1.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna about people who offer sacrifice full of faith but set aside the rules of the scriptures. Is their state pure, passionate or dark?

17-2.kid: Krishna says the faith of every person comes from their own nature, and it is of three kinds: pure, passionate and dark. He asks Arjuna to hear about them.

17-3.kid: Krishna says each person's faith matches their own nature. A person is made of their faith: whatever their faith is, that is what they are.

17-4.kid: Krishna says pure people worship the Gods. Passionate people worship gnomes and giants. Dark people worship ghosts and crowds of spirits.

17-5.kid: Krishna speaks of people who put themselves through harsh, painful practices that the scriptures do not ask for. They do it out of vanity and pride, pushed by strong desires.

17-6.kid: Krishna says such unwise people torment their own bodies, and torment him too, for he lives within the body. He calls their purpose demon-like.

17-7.kid: Krishna says the food each person likes is also of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, self-discipline and giving. He asks Arjuna to hear how they differ.

17-8.kid: Krishna says pure people like foods that add life, energy, strength, health and cheerfulness. These foods are tasty, filling and pleasant.

17-9.kid: Krishna says passionate people like foods that are bitter, sour, salty, too hot, spicy, dry and burning. Such foods bring pain, sadness and sickness.

17-10.kid: Krishna says dark people like food that is stale, tasteless, rotten, left over and unclean.

17-11.kid: Krishna says a sacrifice is pure when people offer it as the rules say, wanting no reward, simply because it ought to be done.

17-12.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that a sacrifice offered to gain a reward, or to show off, is passionate.

17-13.kid: Krishna says a sacrifice is dark when it ignores the rules, shares no food, has no sacred words and no gifts, and is empty of faith.

17-14.kid: Krishna says self-discipline of the body means honouring the Gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise, and being pure, straightforward, self-controlled and never harming anyone.

17-15.kid: Krishna says self-discipline of speech means words that are true, pleasant and helpful and upset no one, along with regular study of the scriptures.

17-16.kid: Krishna says self-discipline of the mind is a peaceful mind, silence, self-control and a pure, honest heart.

17-17.kid: Krishna says that when steady people practise these three kinds of self-discipline with great faith, wanting no reward, it is called pure.

17-18.kid: Krishna says self-discipline practised to win respect, honour and worship, or to show off, is passionate. It is unsteady and does not last.

17-19.kid: Krishna says self-discipline practised out of foolish thinking, by hurting oneself, or to harm another person, is called dark.

17-20.kid: Krishna says a gift is pure when it is given because giving is right, at a fitting place and time, to a worthy person who gives nothing back.

17-21.kid: Krishna says a gift is passionate when it is given hoping to get something back, or looking for a reward, or given unwillingly.

17-22.kid: Krishna says a gift is dark when it is given at the wrong place or time, to unworthy people, without respect or with scorn.

17-23.kid: Krishna says the words Om, Tat, Sat have been known as the three-part name of the Eternal. By it, long ago, the Brahmanas, the Vedas and sacrifices were made.

17-24.kid: Krishna says this is why acts of sacrifice, giving and self-discipline, as the rules lay down, are always begun by saying Om.

17-25.kid: Krishna says those who seek to be set free say Tat, and do their many acts of sacrifice, self-discipline and giving without aiming for any reward.

17-26.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the word Sat is used to mean what is real and what is good. It is also used for a good deed.

17-27.kid: Krishna says being steady in sacrifice, self-discipline and giving is also called Sat. Action done for the sake of the Supreme is called Sat too.

17-28.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that whatever is offered, given or done, and any self-discipline practised, without faith is called Asat. It is worth nothing, in this world or the next.

18-1.kid: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain, each one separately, the true meaning of renunciation and of relinquishment.

18-2.kid: Krishna says the sages call it renunciation when someone gives up actions done out of desire. The wise call it relinquishment when someone lets go of the results of all actions.

18-3.kid: Krishna says some thinkers declare that action should be given up as an evil. Others say acts of sacrifice, giving and self-discipline should not be given up.

18-4.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna to hear his final word on relinquishment, or letting go, which has been explained as being of three kinds.

18-5.kid: Krishna says acts of sacrifice, giving and self-discipline should not be given up but should be done, because they make the wise pure.

18-6.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that even these acts should be done without clinging to them or to their results. This is his firm and best belief.

18-7.kid: Krishna says it is not right to give up actions that are one's duty. To give them up out of confusion is called dark.

18-8.kid: Krishna says someone who gives up an action because it is painful, fearing trouble for the body, lets go in a passionate way, and does not get the fruit of letting go.

18-9.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that doing a required duty only because it ought to be done, letting go of clinging and of the results, is pure letting go.

18-10.kid: Krishna says a pure person who lets go, with steady understanding and no doubts left, does not hate unpleasant work and does not cling to pleasant work.

18-11.kid: Krishna says no one with a body can give up action completely. The one who lets go of the results of action is called a relinquisher.

18-12.kid: Krishna says that those who do not let go receive the fruit of their actions after death, good, bad or mixed. Those who let go receive none.

18-13.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna to learn from him the five causes behind every action, as a teaching of wisdom has explained them.

18-14.kid: Krishna names the five causes: the body, the doer, the senses, the many kinds of energy at work, and fifth, the presiding divinity.

18-15.kid: Krishna says that whatever a person does with body, speech or mind, whether right or wrong, these five are its causes.

18-16.kid: Krishna says that, this being so, a person with an untrained mind who sees his own Self as the doer has a twisted view and does not see.

18-17.kid: Krishna says that a person free from self-importance, whose mind is untouched, does not kill even though he kills these people, and he is not bound by it.

18-18.kid: Krishna says knowledge, what is known and the knower are what move us to act. The means, the deed and the doer are the three parts of action.

18-19.kid: Krishna says knowledge, action and the doer are also each of three kinds, according to the qualities. He asks Arjuna to hear about these too.

18-20.kid: Krishna says knowledge is pure when it sees in all beings the one that can never be destroyed, undivided in all that is divided.

18-21.kid: Krishna says knowledge is passionate when it sees all beings as many separate things, each different from the others.

18-22.kid: Krishna says knowledge is dark when it clings to one small thing as if it were the whole, without reason, without truth, narrow and small.

18-23.kid: Krishna says an action is pure when it is a set duty, done without love or hate, by someone who wants no reward and does not cling.

18-24.kid: Krishna says an action is passionate when it is done out of longing for what one wants, or with pride, or with great strain.

18-25.kid: Krishna says an action is dark when it is started out of confusion, without thinking of the results, the loss, the harm to others or one's own ability.

18-26.kid: Krishna says a doer is pure who does not cling, is not full of himself, is steady and strong-hearted, and stays the same in success or failure.

18-27.kid: Krishna says a doer is passionate who is full of desire, wants the rewards of action, is greedy, harmful and impure, and is tossed between joy and sorrow.

18-28.kid: Krishna says a doer is dark who is unsettled, crude, stubborn, dishonest, spiteful, lazy, gloomy and always putting things off.

18-29.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to hear how understanding and firmness are each of three kinds, according to the qualities, as he explains them fully, one by one.

18-30.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that understanding is pure when it knows when to act and when to hold back, what to do and not do, fear and fearlessness, being bound and being free.

18-31.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that understanding is passionate when it gets right and wrong, and what should and should not be done, all mixed up.

18-32.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that understanding is dark when, wrapped in darkness, it thinks wrong is right and sees everything upside down.

18-33.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that firmness is pure when, through yoga, it steadily holds back the work of the mind, the breath and the senses, never wavering.

18-34.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that firmness is passionate when someone holds tight to duty, desire and wealth, clinging to them and wanting their rewards.

18-35.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that firmness is dark when a foolish person will not give up sleep, fear, grief, despair and pride.

18-36.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna to hear about the three kinds of happiness. One kind is enjoyed through practice, and it brings an end to pain.

18-37.kid: Krishna says happiness that is like poison at first but like nectar in the end is pure. It comes from knowing the Self.

18-38.kid: Krishna says happiness that comes when the senses meet their objects is passionate. It is like nectar at first but like poison in the end.

18-39.kid: Krishna says happiness that fools a person from start to finish is dark. It comes from sleep, laziness and carelessness.

18-40.kid: Krishna says there is nothing on earth, or among the Shining Ones in heaven, that is free from these three qualities born of matter.

18-41.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the duties of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Sudras are divided according to the qualities born of their own nature.

18-42.kid: Krishna says the duties of the Brahmanas, born of their own nature, are self-control, self-discipline, purity, forgiveness, honesty, knowledge, wisdom and belief.

18-43.kid: Krishna says the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of their own nature, are bravery, firmness, skill, not running from battle, generosity and the nature of a ruler.

18-44.kid: Krishna says farming, caring for cattle and trade are the duty of the Vaishyas, born of their own nature. Work of service is the duty of the Sudras, born of their own nature.

18-45.kid: Krishna says a person reaches perfection by being devoted to his own duty. He asks Arjuna to hear how that perfection is won.

18-46.kid: Krishna says a person wins perfection by worshipping Him through his own duty: Him from whom all beings come, and by whom all this is filled.

18-47.kid: Krishna says one's own duty, even done imperfectly, is better than another's duty done well. Whoever does the duty set by his own nature does no wrong.

18-48.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that one should not give up the duty one is born to, even with its faults, for all work is clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.

18-49.kid: Krishna says one whose mind clings to nothing, who has mastered himself and whose desires are gone, reaches through renunciation the highest perfection of freedom.

18-50.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to learn from him, in brief, how one who has reached perfection reaches the Eternal, the highest point of wisdom.

18-51.kid: Krishna describes such a person: pure in understanding, controlling himself with firmness, letting go of sounds and other things of the senses, and putting aside strong liking and hatred.

18-52.kid: Krishna goes on: such a person lives in a quiet, lonely place, eats little, controls speech, body and mind, is always deep in meditation, and stays free from longing.

18-53.kid: Krishna says that once such a person gives up self-importance, force, pride, desire, anger and greed, and is unselfish and peaceful, he is fit to become the Eternal.

18-54.kid: Krishna says one who has become the Eternal is peaceful within, and neither grieves nor longs for anything. He is the same to all beings, and gains the highest devotion to Krishna.

18-55.kid: Krishna says that by devotion such a person truly knows who and what Krishna is. Then, knowing him truly, he at once enters into the Supreme.

18-56.kid: Krishna says that a person who takes shelter in him, even while always doing all kinds of work, reaches by his grace the eternal, unending state.

18-57.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna to give all his works to Krishna in his mind, to make Krishna his goal, to use the yoga of wise understanding, and always to keep his thoughts on Krishna.

18-58.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that if he fixes his mind on Krishna, he will overcome every obstacle by the grace of Krishna. But if pride stops him from listening, he will be destroyed.

18-59.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that if pride makes him think, 'I will not fight,' that decision is useless. His own nature will force him anyway.

18-60.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that he is bound by his own duty, born of his own nature. What he does not want to do, out of confusion, he will do even against his will.

18-61.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna that the Lord lives in the hearts of all beings and, by his power of illusion, makes them all turn, as if they were set on a turning wheel.

18-62.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to go to the Lord for shelter with all his heart. By the grace of the Lord, Arjuna will find the highest peace and the home that lasts forever.

18-63.kid: Krishna says he has now told Arjuna wisdom deeper than any secret. He tells Arjuna to think it all over fully, and then to do as he wishes.

18-64.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen once more to his highest word, the deepest of all. Because Arjuna is very dear to him, he will say what is good for Arjuna.

18-65.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to fill his mind with Krishna, be devoted to him, offer sacrifice to him and bow down to him. He promises that Arjuna, who is dear to him, will come to him.

18-66.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna to give up all duties and come to him alone for shelter. He tells Arjuna not to grieve, for he will free him from all sins.

18-67.kid: Krishna tells Arjuna never to share this teaching with anyone who lacks self-discipline or devotion, who is unwilling, or who speaks ill of Krishna.

18-68.kid: Krishna says that whoever, with the highest devotion to him, teaches this deep secret to his devotees will surely come to him.

18-69.kid: Krishna says no one among people does him dearer service than such a person, and no one on earth will ever be dearer to him.

18-70.kid: Krishna says that whoever studies this holy conversation between them will be worshipping him with the sacrifice of wisdom. That is his belief.

18-71.kid: Krishna says that even a person who simply hears this teaching with faith and without ill will is set free, and reaches the happy worlds of those who do right.

18-72.kid: Krishna asks Arjuna if he has listened to all this with a focused mind, and if his confusion, born of not knowing, is now gone.

18-73.kid: Arjuna says his confusion is gone, by the grace of Krishna. He stands firm, his doubts have left him, and he will do as Krishna says.

18-74.kid: Sanjaya says he has heard this wonderful conversation between Krishna and the great-souled Arjuna, and it made his hair stand on end.

18-75.kid: Sanjaya says that by the grace of Vyasa he heard this secret, highest yoga straight from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, speaking it himself.

18-76.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that as he remembers, again and again, this wonderful and holy conversation between Krishna and Arjuna, he rejoices again and again.

18-77.kid: Sanjaya tells the king that as he remembers, again and again, that most wonderful form of Hari, his wonder is great, and he feels joy again and again.

18-78.kid: Sanjaya says that wherever Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and Arjuna, the archer, are found, there will be prosperity, victory and other good things. That is what he believes.
